_comment: Phase 3E Indonesian dish foundation. Every entry here is a DECOMPOSITION HINT, not a recipe: it lists what a compound dish is typically made of, so that a future image-based estimator can look for and estimate each visible component separately (each component is then matched against data/foods.json / USDA like any other detected food). NO entry may carry calories/protein/fat/carbs or any gram amount - services/dish_matcher.py enforces this at load time. 'variability' is one of: 'fixed_components' (a stable, enumerable set of parts - though individual components may still be marked optional), 'ambiguous' (the bare name alone does not determine which distinct dish is meant), or 'variable' (composition varies too much to enumerate - only a category description is given). This is NOT wired into bot.py or Gemini in this phase.

dishes.name: Pecel lele

components.notes: usually sambal bawang or sambal terasi
commonly served alongside but sold/ordered separately; detect and match independently

dishes.notes: The fish, sambal, and raw vegetables (lalapan) are the defining parts; rice is a separate, independently-detectable staple, not part of the dish itself.

dishes.name: Nasi uduk

components.notes: rice cooked in coconut milk; nutritionally distinct from plain nasi putih - do not conflate the two
one of several common accompaniments, not guaranteed present

dishes.notes: Only the coconut-milk rice itself is guaranteed present. It is conventionally sold as a plate with a vendor-chosen selection of side dishes - closer to nasi padang's variability than to pecel lele's fixed set, so every side beyond the rice is marked optional and must be detected, not assumed.

dishes.name: Martabak telur

components.notes: minced beef or chicken, common but not universal
thin curry sauce for dipping, sometimes served alongside

dishes.notes: Savory. Nutritionally very different from martabak manis - never conflate the two under a bare 'martabak' match.

dishes.name: Martabak manis

components.notes: thick, sweet, yeasted pancake, cooked in a heavy pan; folded over its topping

VARIABLE - common toppings include cokelat meses, keju parut, kacang tanah cincang, susu kental manis, wijen, in any combination; the specific topping(s) present must be detected individually, never assumed

dishes.notes: Sweet. Nutritionally very different from martabak telur - never conflate the two under a bare 'martabak' match. The topping combination varies per order and materially changes sugar/fat content, so it is deliberately not enumerated as a fixed list.

dishes.name: Nasi goreng

components.notes: fried rice base, already seasoned; nutritionally distinct from plain nasi putih
ceplok, dadar, or orak-arik style; common but not universal
protein mix-in varies widely by vendor/order

dishes.notes: The rice itself is already a composite (cooked with seasoning, sometimes small mix-ins) - treat 'nasi goreng' as its own staple, not as plain rice plus separate seasoning.

dishes.name: Mie ayam

components.notes: wheat noodles, usually tossed in seasoned oil
diced or shredded chicken in sweet soy seasoning, the defining topping
fried or boiled wonton, commonly included
served separately (mie ayam kuah) or omitted (mie ayam kering/'mie ayam yamin')

dishes.notes: Whether broth is served in the bowl or on the side (or not at all) varies by vendor/order and changes the dish substantially - it is marked optional rather than assumed.

dishes.name: Bakso

components.notes: beef (or mixed) meatball, the defining component
clear beef broth, almost always present
wheat noodles or rice vermicelli, common but not universal
often tahu bakso (tofu stuffed with meatball mixture)

dishes.notes: Meatball count/size and which extras are included both vary widely by vendor and order.

dishes.name: Soto ayam

components.notes: glass or rice vermicelli, common but not universal
commonly served alongside but sold/ordered separately; detect and match independently

dishes.notes: Regional variants (Lamongan, Kudus, Betawi, ...) differ further in broth style and add-ins; this lists the common core, not an exhaustive or fixed recipe.

dishes.name: Gado-gado

components.notes: peanut sauce, the defining component, coats everything
mixed boiled vegetables - typically some of kol, tauge, kacang panjang, kangkung, kentang; exact mix varies
fried or boiled tofu, commonly included
fried or boiled tempeh, commonly included

dishes.notes: The exact vegetable mix and which proteins/staples are included both vary by vendor and order; only the peanut sauce and 'some mixed boiled vegetables' are near-universal.

dishes.name: Ketoprak

components.notes: compressed rice cake, the defining staple

dishes.notes: Closely related to gado-gado but built on ketupat/lontong + tahu + peanut sauce as the near-fixed core, rather than gado-gado's mixed-vegetable emphasis.

dishes.name: Nasi padang

components.notes: EXAMPLE ONLY, not exhaustive: rendang, ayam pop, ayam bakar, gulai tunjang, gulai ikan, dendeng balado, paru goreng, sayur singkong, sayur nangka, sambal ijo, perkedel, telur dadar - a plate typically has several of these, chosen per vendor/order

dishes.notes: This is a MEAL CATEGORY, not a dish with a fixed identity beyond rice: the selection, number, and portion of side dishes (lauk) varies enormously by vendor and by what the customer chooses. Each visible lauk on the plate must be detected and matched as its own separate food - never assume a 'standard' nasi padang composition.

dishes.name: Martabak
dishes.notes: Bare 'martabak' does not say whether this is the savory egg-and-meat martabak telur or the sweet martabak manis - the two are nutritionally very different (savory fried dough with egg/meat filling vs. a sugary, buttery sweet pancake with rich toppings). This entry must never be silently resolved to either specific dish; a caller must ask for clarification or use additional visual evidence (color, shape, presence of chocolate/toppings vs. visible egg/meat filling) to pick martabak_telur or martabak_manis explicitly.
